title: Transpose a Matrix
statement:
You are given a matrix with `r` rows and `c` columns. Print its **transpose**: the matrix with `c` rows and `r` columns in which the element at row `j`, column `i` is the element that was at row `i`, column `j` of the original. In other words, rows become columns and columns become rows.

The matrix is not necessarily square, so the shape of the result differs from the shape of the input.

**Follow-up:** If the matrix is square (`r = c`), can you transpose it in place, by swapping elements across the main diagonal, without allocating a second matrix? Why does this not work in place for a non-square matrix?
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `r` and `c`.
Each of the next `r` lines contains `c` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the transposed matrix: `c` lines, each with `r` space-separated integers.

examples.explanation: The first column of the input (1, 4) becomes the first row of the output, and so on. A 2x3 matrix becomes a 3x2 matrix.
For a square matrix the diagonal (1, 5, 9) stays put and elements mirror across it.
A single row becomes a single column.

hints: Look at where element (i, j) of the input must end up in the output.
The output has `c` rows; row `j` of the output is column `j` of the input read top to bottom.
For a square matrix you can swap `a[i][j]` and `a[j][i]` for every `i < j` to do it in place.
